The test `test_min_max_only_nan` checks whether the `min` and `max` methods of a Categorical object work correctly when all values are NaN. However, the test failure indicates that this is not the case.

Following the execution path, we find that the error occurs in the `_values_for_argsort` method of the Categorical class (line 2187 in pandas/core/arrays/categorical.py), which tries to calculate the minimum value of the categorical values using `self._codes.min()`. This method is called by the `min` method of the Categorical object.

However, looking at the code snippet for the `__init__` method of the Categorical class (lines 312-391 in pandas/core/arrays/categorical.py), we can see that when creating a categorical object with ordered categories, the `_codes` attribute is set to an array of codes using the `coerce_indexer_dtype` function. If all values are NaN, this array will be empty.

The error message indicates that there's a problem trying to reduce an array of size zero (line 34 in numpy/core/_methods.py). This suggests that the issue lies in how the categorical object handles NaN values when calculating the minimum or maximum value.

Consequently, un-escaped strings are being returned, which leads to the error demonstrated by the test.
